RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 25

An all-female panel alone is not evidence of discrimination; panel composition typically reflects organizational demographics. Bringing up the interviewers' sex will undermine your credibility and appear as an unfounded accusation.

While subconscious bias or in-group affinity is always a possibility, paper qualifications—such as your master's degree and administrative experience—are only part of the hiring decision. Leadership appointments rely heavily on interview evaluations, strategic vision, interpersonal fit, and reference checks. 

Do not raise the panel's gender. Instead, follow up professionally on your requested written explanation. If you choose to formally challenge the decision, base your case entirely on objective merit, scoring matrices, and procedural fairness.
